_comment: Everyday Finnish A1, planned with Tung 2026-10-24 (see SERIES_BIBLE.md). Episodes are added chapter by chapter; ids must stay unique.

summer.look: late summer: full green leafy trees, bright sunshine, long light evenings, flowers in yards and planters.
summer.sounds: birdsong, a light breeze in the leaves

autumn.look: trees turning yellow, orange and red, fallen leaves on paths and pavements, grey skies or low golden light, wet streets and puddles after rain, dusk coming early.
autumn.sounds: rain on umbrellas or windows, leaves rustling underfoot, gusts of wind

winter.look: snow on the ground, roofs and bare trees, short days under a dark-blue sky with warm yellow street lights and lit windows already in the afternoon, breath steaming in the cold, candles in windows.
winter.sounds: snow crunching underfoot, cold wind, a door shutting out the cold, boots stamped off on a mat

spring.look: the last snow melting into puddles, bare trees with the first light-green buds and leaves, bright sun, long light evenings returning, early flowers.
spring.sounds: meltwater dripping, birdsong returning, bicycles on the street

episodes.title: Moi!
episodes.description: Alex astuu ensimmäisenä aamuna uuden kotitalonsa pihalle ja on matkalla töihin. Naapuri Linnea, nuori opiskelija, on lähdössä pyörällä yliopistolle ja sanoo hänelle iloisesti: Moi! Alex ja Linnea kertovat nimensä toisilleen englanniksi. Linnea opettaa Alexille, miten suomalaiset sanovat moi, huomenta ja hei hei arjessa. Alex toistaa sanat huolellisesti ja lähtee töihin sanoen: Hei hei!
episodes.notes: First meeting: Alex and Linnea, who lives in the same building and studies at the university, exchange names in English (the Finnish for introducing yourself is taught in episode 6). Linnea speaks clear, relaxed Finnish and slows down for Alex; he repeats after her. Late August, Alex's first morning in the building.
episodes.illustration_scene: A sunny late-summer morning in the leafy courtyard of a Helsinki apartment building. Alex, a young man in a hoodie, stands chatting with Linnea, a student about to cycle to the university; her bicycle is beside her with books in the basket. Both smile and use friendly gestures. A path, flowers and the building entrance are in the background.
episodes.when: late August

episodes.title: Kiitos!
episodes.description: Linnea vie Alexin kulman kahvilaan ja neuvoo häntä englanniksi, kun Alex tilaa ensimmäisen kahvinsa. Baristan nimi on Sanni, ja hän kertoo sen englanniksi. Sanni kysyy, haluaako Alex maitoa kahviinsa, ja Linnea opettaa Alexille sanat kyllä ja ei. Kun Sanni ojentaa kahvin ja sanoo ole hyvä, Alex sanoo kiitos. Sitten Alex törmää vahingossa sokeritelineeseen ja pyytää anteeksi.
episodes.notes: Linnea is Alex's friend and the guide: she coaches him in English and teaches the four phrases. Sanni, the barista, has short service lines only (asks about milk, hands over the coffee) and never teaches. Alex and Sanni have never met; Sanni says her name in English. Sanni says 'Ole hyvä' when handing over the coffee but it is not drilled (four taught phrases is the limit).
episodes.illustration_scene: The counter of a cosy Helsinki café on a bright morning. Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde ponytail, stands beside Alex, a young man in a hoodie, who is holding a coffee cup and looks slightly unsure; she smiles encouragingly. Sanni, the barista, stands behind the counter with a friendly smile. Behind them are coffee machines, pastries under glass and a small sugar stand at the end of the counter.
episodes.when: late August

episodes.title: Hitaammin, kiitos!
episodes.description: Alex ja Linnea istuvat aamulla bussissa matkalla keskustaan. Linnea alkaa innoissaan kertoa viikonlopustaan nopeasti suomeksi, eikä Alex ymmärrä melkein mitään. Linnea opettaa Alexille, miten hän voi pelastaa keskustelun: sanomalla en ymmärrä, pyytämällä puhumaan hitaammin ja pyytämällä vielä kerran. Alex kokeilee kaikkia kolmea, ja Linnea toistaa kertomuksensa hitaasti.
episodes.notes: Alex and Linnea already know each other from episode 1 (same building): no introductions. Linnea is the guide and also the fast talker: she chats in quick puhekieli, Alex gets lost, then learns three rescue phrases and uses them. Alex has already learned 'Anteeksi' (episode 2) and may use it, but it is not retaught. A morning bus ride into the city, early September.
episodes.illustration_scene: Two friends side by side on a city bus seat on a bright morning. Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde ponytail, talks animatedly with both hands in the air; Alex, a young man in a hoodie, listens with a puzzled, polite smile and raised eyebrows. Other seats, handrails and a window with city buildings passing by are visible. No other passengers.
episodes.when: early September

episodes.title: Mikä tämä on?
episodes.description: Alex tulee Linnean kanssa samaan kahvilaan kuin viimeksi, ja Sanni tunnistaa hänet. Alex osoittaa lasin alla olevaa leivonnaista ja kysyy Linnean opastamana: Mikä tämä on? Sitten hän kysyy, missä vessa on, ja lopuksi hän osoittaa seinällä olevaa muotokuvaa ja kysyy: Kuka tuo on? Sanni vastaa lyhyesti, ja Linnea selittää, mitä kukin kysymyssana tarkoittaa.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide. Sanni, the barista, has short service answers only and never teaches; she recognises Alex from episode 2 and already knows Linnea. Each question word is taught on a real thing in the café: a pastry (mikä), the toilet (missä), a framed portrait of the composer Sibelius on the wall (kuka; Sanni says it is Sibelius, Finland's famous composer).
episodes.illustration_scene: The inside of a cosy Helsinki café. Alex, a young man in a hoodie, stands at the glass pastry display pointing at one round cinnamon bun with a curious look; Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde ponytail, stands beside him smiling and encouraging; Sanni, the barista with a dark bob haircut and a black top, is clearly visible behind the counter with a friendly nod. The pastries sit on plain trays with NO labels, NO price tags, no menu boards, no chalkboards and no signs anywhere. On the wall behind them hangs one framed painted portrait of a stern elderly man with white hair (a painting, with no plaque or caption). A door to the side leads towards the toilets.
episodes.when: early September

episodes.title: Yksi vesi, kiitos
episodes.description: Linnea ja Alex kävelevät kadulla, ja Alex on janoinen. Linnea vie hänet pieneen kioskiin, jossa myyjä Markku on kiireinen ja puhuu nopeasti. Linnea opettaa Alexille, miten ostetaan yksi asia: yksi vesi, kiitos, kysytään hinta sanalla paljonko ja maksetaan sanoen tässä. Alex tekee ostoksen itse, ja Markku vastaa lyhyesti ja nopeasti.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide. Markku, the kiosk vendor, is busy and clipped with short service lines only, and never teaches; he and Alex have never met and no names are exchanged. Markku says the price in Finnish ('kaksi euroa'); Linnea glosses it in English, numbers are not taught yet (episode 8). Alex has learned 'Kiitos' in episode 2 and uses it at the end, but it is not retaught.
episodes.illustration_scene: A small street kiosk on a sunny Helsinki street. Markku, the kiosk vendor, leans out of the kiosk window handing over a bottle of water, looking busy. Alex, a young man in a hoodie, holds out a coin; Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde ponytail, stands next to Alex with an encouraging smile. Drinks and snacks are on shelves inside the kiosk, a bicycle leans against the wall. No signs, prices or writing.
episodes.when: a warm day in early September

episodes.title: Mä oon Anna
episodes.description: Alex kantaa iltapäivällä isoa pahvilaatikkoa kotitalonsa ovelle, ja yläkerran naapuri Anna pitää ovea auki hänelle. He eivät ole tavanneet ennen. Alex on harjoitellut esittäytymistä yksin ja kysyy Annalta, saako hän kokeilla: Minä olen Alex. Mikä sinun nimi on? Anna vastaa iloisesti puhekielellä: Mä oon Anna. Hauska tutustua! Alex huomaa, että Anna sanoo mä ja oon eikä minä ja olen, ja Anna selittää englanniksi, että kirjassa sanotaan minä olen, mutta arjessa suomalaiset sanovat mä oon. Lopuksi he kantavat laatikon yhdessä hissille.
episodes.notes: First meeting of Alex and Anna: they have never met and neither knows the other's name until they say it here. Anna is the guide (a friendly neighbour in her fifties, patient and clear). The reason for the scene is the heavy box, not a lesson: Alex has been practising his introduction from a book and wants to try it on a real person, so he asks Anna to check it; she answers naturally in spoken Finnish and that contrast (minä olen / mä oon) is the point. Label the forms right: 'minä olen' is the book/standard form, 'mä oon' the everyday spoken one. Alex keeps speaking careful standard Finnish; he does not switch to mä/oon. 'Moi' (episode 1) may be used as a callback but is not retaught. Early September, a sunny late afternoon.
episodes.illustration_scene: The front door of a Helsinki apartment building on a sunny late afternoon. Alex, a young man, carries a big plain cardboard box with both arms and peeks round it; Anna, a friendly neighbour in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair, holds the heavy wooden door open for him with one hand and a cloth shopping bag in the other, smiling. Green trees, a bicycle rack and flower planters in the courtyard behind them. The box is plain with no print or writing.
episodes.when: early September

episodes.title: Mistä sä oot?
episodes.description: On sateinen syyskuun iltapäivä, ja Alex ja Linnea juoksevat sadetta pakoon kaupungin kirjastoon. He ripustavat märät sadetakit ja istuvat ikkunan viereen. Linnea kertoo, että hänen opiskelijakavereillaan on lauantaina ilta, ja Alex on kutsuttu. Siellä kaikki kysyvät häneltä suomeksi: Mistä sä oot? Linnea näyttää, miten Alex voi vastata: Minä olen Brasiliasta ja Minä asun Helsingissä, ja miten hän voi kysyä takaisin: Entä sinä? Linnea kertoo olevansa Oulusta.
episodes.notes: Alex and Linnea are friends (episodes 1-5): no introductions. Linnea is the guide. The reason is the student party on Saturday, where people will ask him where he is from; they practise it as a quick, fun rehearsal, Linnea playing a curious partygoer. Alex is from Brazil and lives in Helsinki; Linnea is from Oulu and moved to Helsinki for university ('Mä oon Oulusta' may come up as her answer, glossed). Linnea asks in spoken Finnish ('Mistä sä oot?'), Alex answers in careful standard Finnish ('Minä olen...'); name the difference once in passing, it was explained in episode 6. Late September: they come in from the rain with wet jackets; it is the first properly autumn day of the series. Quiet voices: they are in a library.
episodes.illustration_scene: A big bright modern city library on a rainy late-September afternoon. Alex and Linnea sit side by side at a long wooden table by a huge window streaked with rain; outside, trees are turning yellow and orange in the rain, with wet leaves on an empty square. Their wet raincoats hang on the backs of their chairs. Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde braid, leans in playfully as if asking a question; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, answers with a shy grin. Shelves of books with plain spines, no titles, no writing.
episodes.when: late September

episodes.title: Yksi, kaksi, kolme
episodes.description: Sateinen lokakuun ilta. Anna tulee kauppakassien kanssa kotitalon ovelle samaan aikaan kuin Alex, eikä hän saa käsiään vapaaksi. Hän pyytää Alexia näppäilemään ovikoodin ja sanoo numerot ääneen suomeksi: kaksi, nolla, viisi, yhdeksän. Alex kuuntelee tarkasti ja näppäilee koodin. He menevät hissillä ylös ja juttelevat sateesta. Annan ovella Anna tarjoaa Alexille omenoita kesämökkinsä puusta ja kysyy: Montako? Alex vastaa varovasti suomeksi, Anna nauraa ja antaa kymmenen, ja he laskevat omenat yhdessä pussiin yhdestä kymmeneen.
episodes.notes: Alex and Anna are neighbours who met in episode 6: no introductions, they use each other's names. Anna is the guide. Numbers come up only where Alex has to HEAR or SAY them, never where he could just read digits: (1) the door code, which Anna says aloud in Finnish because her hands are full, so he must understand each number to type it; (2) the apples from her summer cottage tree at her door: she asks 'Montako?' (how many?, glossed once, not drilled), he answers with a small number in Finnish, she laughs and gives him ten, and they count them into his bag together, Alex saying seven to ten himself. The lift ride is small talk about the rain in English: no numbers are taught on the lift buttons (the buttons show digits, so there would be no reason). Teach the standard numbers; Anna may mention once that in quick speech people say 'yks, kaks' (glossed, not drilled). Alex says 'Kiitos' (episode 2) for the apples, not retaught. The door code is invented and harmless. Early October evening, already dark outside, rain; they shake off umbrellas in the entrance.
episodes.illustration_scene: Inside a small apartment-building lift on a dark, rainy October evening. Anna, a neighbour in her fifties, holds two full paper grocery bags with apples and a baguette poking out and a wet folded umbrella hooked on her arm; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, reaches out to press a round button on the button panel, which shows only plain round buttons with no numbers or symbols. Both smile. Raindrops glisten on their coats. Warm lift light.
episodes.when: a rainy evening in early October

episodes.title: Mitä sä teet?
episodes.description: Aurinkoinen lokakuun lauantai. Alex ja Linnea kävelevät puistossa, jossa puut ovat keltaisia ja punaisia ja lehdet rapisevat jalkojen alla. Alex kertoo, että maanantaina hänen tiiminsä syö yhdessä lounasta ja suomalaiset kollegat varmasti kysyvät häneltä suomeksi: Mitä sä teet? Linnea neuvoo, miten hän vastaa: Minä olen ohjelmoija. Linnea kertoo itsestään: Mä opiskelen. Alex kysyy Linnealta, mitä hän opiskelee, ja Linnea vastaa englanniksi, että biologiaa.
episodes.notes: Alex and Linnea are good friends by now: relaxed banter, no introductions. Linnea is the guide. The reason is the team lunch on Monday at Alex's new job (a small tech company, he is a programmer); Linnea also asks about how the job is going in English. 'Missä sä oot töissä?' (where do you work) is the follow-up question colleagues ask; Alex answers that he works at a small tech company, in English or with a short Finnish answer only if it is taught. Linnea studies biology at the university. Callbacks: 'Mistä sä oot?' (episode 7) may come back. Mid-October, the autumn colours (ruska) are at their best, a crisp sunny day; they kick through leaves.
episodes.illustration_scene: A Helsinki park on a crisp, sunny mid-October Saturday. The trees blaze yellow, orange and red and fallen leaves cover the path. Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, walks beside Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde braid; Alex gestures as if describing something with his hands, Linnea laughs. A wooden bench and a lamp post beside the path, the low autumn sun behind the trees.
episodes.when: a sunny Saturday in mid-October

episodes.title: Missä on apteekki?
episodes.description: Harmaa lokakuun lauantai. Alexilla on flunssa: hän aivastelee ja tarvitsee nenäsuihkeen. Hän ja Linnea nousevat ratikasta keskustassa, ja Alex haluaa löytää apteekin. Linnea näyttää, miten kysytään: Missä on apteekki? ja miten suomalaiset vastaavat: tuolla ja lähellä. Apteekki on lähellä, joten Linnea ehdottaa, että kävellään eikä mennä ratikalla. Apteekin jälkeen he miettivät, miten mennään kotiin, ja Alex sanoo itse: Mennään ratikalla.
episodes.notes: Alex and Linnea are good friends: relaxed banter, no introductions. Linnea is the guide. The reason for the scene is Alex's cold, not a lesson: he needs a pharmacy now. Each phrase is needed in the moment: Alex asks where the pharmacy is ('Missä on vessa?' from episode 4 is the model: 'Missä on...?' is a callback, glossed briefly); Linnea answers the way a Finn would, pointing: 'Tuolla' (over there) and 'Lähellä' (near), so Alex learns to understand the answer; because it is near they walk instead of taking the tram; on the way home Alex suggests the tram himself: 'Mennään ratikalla' (let's take the tram), and Linnea explains that 'ratikka' is what Helsinki people call the tram. No passers-by speak: only Alex and Linnea. Late October: grey, damp, early dusk, wet leaves; Alex has a scarf and a red nose.
episodes.illustration_scene: A Helsinki city-centre street on a grey late-October afternoon, just after rain. A green city tram is pulling away from a stop behind them. Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde braid, points down the street; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair and a slightly red nose, holds a tissue and looks where she points. Down the street, a pharmacy with a plain green cross sign; wet pavement with fallen yellow leaves. Tram, signs and shop fronts carry NO letters, numbers or writing.
episodes.when: a grey Saturday in late October

episodes.title: Taas sä!
episodes.description: Kylmä lokakuun ilta. Alex ja Anna kävelevät kaupasta kotiin, ja Alexin pitää ladata matkakorttiinsa kuukauden lippu kulman kioskista. Myyjä on Markku, joka tunnistaa Alexin: Taas sä! ja kertoo nimensä. Alex kysyy Annan neuvosta: Paljonko kuukausilippu maksaa? Markku vastaa nopeasti: kuusikymmentäneljä euroa. Anna selittää kymmenet: kymmenen, kaksikymmentä, kolmekymmentä ja niin edelleen sataan asti, ja Alex maksaa.
episodes.notes: Anna is the guide (neighbour, patient, clear). Markku, the kiosk vendor, has short, fast service lines only and never teaches. He recognises Alex from episode 5 ('Taas sä!', glossed by Anna) and tells his name this time ('Mä oon Markku'); Alex answers with his own name (episode 6). The numbers are needed because Markku SAYS the price aloud, fast, and Alex must understand it to pay; there is no price display. Alex asks 'Paljonko tämä maksaa?' ('Paljonko?' is from episode 5, now as a full question). Markku says 'kuusikymmentäneljä euroa' (64, an invented price for a month's travel ticket); Alex does not catch it, so Anna breaks it down: tens 'kymmenen, kaksikymmentä, kolmekymmentä...' up to 'sata' (a hundred), then 'kuusikymmentä' + 'neljä'. Alex repeats the price and pays with a card. Numbers 0-10 are from episode 8 (callbacks, not retaught). Markku may say the casual 'kuuskyt' once; Anna glosses it. Late October evening, cold, dark at five; breath steams, warm kiosk light.
episodes.illustration_scene: A small street kiosk lit warmly on a cold, dark late-October evening. Markku, the kiosk vendor, leans out of the kiosk window holding a small card reader; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, holds out a plain travel card; Anna, a neighbour in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair, stands beside him with a cloth shopping bag, smiling. Street lamps glow, wet leaves on the pavement, their breath steams. No signs, prices, numbers or writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a cold evening in late October

lessons_covered: What Time Is It? (mitä kello on)
episodes.title: Mitä kello on?
episodes.description: Sunnuntaiaamu lokakuun lopussa, ja kellot siirrettiin yöllä tunnilla taaksepäin. Alex ja Linnea istuvat tutussa kahvilassa. Alexilla on kello yksitoista videopuhelu kotiin Brasiliaan, mutta hänen puhelimensa akku on loppu, eikä hän ole varma, onko hänen rannekellonsa oikeassa ajassa. Linnea neuvoo häntä kysymään Sannilta: Anteeksi, mitä kello on? Sanni vastaa: Kello on kymmenen. Linnea selittää, että puoli yksitoista tarkoittaa puoli tuntia ennen yhtätoista, ja Alex lähtee ajoissa.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide. Sanni, the barista, knows them both (he is becoming a regular) and only answers briefly; she never teaches. The reason is real: Alex's phone is dead, he has a video call home at eleven, and the clocks went back an hour last night, so he does not trust his old wristwatch (it still shows the summer time). He asks Sanni the time ('Anteeksi' from episode 2 is a callback). Sanni says 'Kello on kymmenen'. Alex says he must leave at half past ten; Linnea teaches 'puoli yksitoista' and explains that Finns say 'half eleven' for 10:30, which surprises him. 'Yksitoista' (eleven) is glossed in passing, not drilled. Season: late October, the first Sunday of winter time, grey and dark outside the café window; candles on the tables.
episodes.illustration_scene: Inside a cosy Helsinki café on a grey late-October Sunday morning, candles on the tables and dark rainy trees outside the window. Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, holds up his wrist and frowns at an old wristwatch; Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde braid, sits opposite him with a coffee and laughs; Sanni, the barista with a dark bob, stands behind the counter. No clocks on the walls. No writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a late-October Sunday morning, the day the clocks went back

episodes.title: Tiistaina illalla
episodes.description: Arki-ilta lokakuun lopussa. Alex kantaa likapyykkikassia talon kellariin, koska hänen asunnossaan ei ole pesukonetta. Pesutuvassa on Anna, joka näyttää hänelle varauslistan. Alex kysyy: Mikä päivä tänään on? Anna kertoo viikonpäivät ja sen, milloin pesutupa on vapaana: maanantaina aamulla, tiistaina illalla. Anna kertoo myös omasta viikostaan: perjantaina illalla hän menee taloyhtiön saunaan. Alex varaa vuoron tiistaiksi illaksi.
episodes.notes: Anna is the guide (neighbour, patient). The reason is real: Alex has no washing machine in his flat and must book the building's shared laundry room in the basement; the booking board has a row for each weekday and a morning and an evening slot, and Anna is there doing her own washing. The days are needed because Anna tells him which slots are free; 'aamulla' (in the morning) and 'illalla' (in the evening) because each day has two slots. Alex picks 'tiistaina illalla' (Tuesday evening). Anna mentions her own week in passing (sauna in the building on Friday evenings, a very Finnish routine) so the days come up again; 'sauna' needs no gloss. Today is Monday. Teach the days in two groups. The booking board is drawn without writing. Late October, dark outside; washing machines hum.
episodes.illustration_scene: A tidy shared laundry room in the basement of a Helsinki apartment building, late-October evening, a small high window shows darkness. Two white washing machines, one running, a drying rack and a wooden bench. Anna, a neighbour in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair, holds a folded towel and points at a plain booking board on the wall with rows of small empty squares and some coloured pegs, no writing; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, holds a full laundry bag and looks at the board. No letters, numbers or writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a Monday evening at the end of October

episodes.title: Milloin nähdään?
episodes.description: Alex ja Linnea ovat kaupungin kirjastossa. Linnealla on tentti marraskuussa, ja Alex haluaa harjoitella suomea, joten he päättävät opiskella yhdessä joka viikko. Linnea kysyy: Milloin nähdään? Alex ehdottaa torstaita, ja Linnea vastaa: torstaina kello viisi. Alex kysyy, kuinka kauan, ja Linnea sanoo: kaksi tuntia. Lopuksi Linnea näyttää, että kirjaston opiskeluhuone varataan aina kahdeksi tunniksi.
episodes.notes: Alex and Linnea are good friends. Linnea is the guide. The reason is real: Linnea has an exam in November and Alex wants regular practice, so they agree a weekly study time and book a library study room, which is booked in two-hour blocks. Each phrase is needed to settle the plan: when ('Milloin nähdään?'), the day and hour ('torstaina kello viisi', using 'torstaina' from episode 13 and 'kello' from episode 12), how long ('Kuinka kauan?'), the answer ('kaksi tuntia'). Linnea may mention that in writing and timetables Finns use the 24-hour clock ('seitsemäntoista' for 17), glossed once, not drilled. Quiet voices: library. Last days of October, dark at five, rain on the big windows.
episodes.illustration_scene: A big bright modern city library on a dark late-October afternoon, rain streaking the huge windows and city lights outside. Alex and Linnea sit at a long wooden table with notebooks and two cups; Linnea, a student with glasses and a blonde braid, holds up two fingers; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, writes in a notebook. Their raincoats hang on the chairs. Shelves of books with plain spines. No writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a rainy afternoon in the last days of October

episodes.title: Hyvää syntymäpäivää!
episodes.description: Anna kutsuu Alexin kahville, koska hän on leiponut täytekakun. Keittiössä Alex huomaa, että kakussa on kynttilöitä, ja kysyy, onko tänään erityinen päivä. Anna kertoo, että tänään on hänen syntymäpäivänsä. Alex sanoo: Hyvää syntymäpäivää! Anna kysyy Alexilta: Milloin sun syntymäpäivä on? Alex vastaa: toukokuussa. Anna kertoo kuukaudet ja sen, että hänen syntymäpäivänsä on aina lokakuussa, kun ruska on jo ohi.
episodes.notes: Anna is the guide. The reason is real: Anna has baked a cream cake and asks Alex for coffee without saying why; the candles give it away, and Alex wants to wish her happy birthday properly. Then birthdays lead to months: Anna asks when his birthday is (spoken 'sun'), he answers 'toukokuussa' (in May); hers is 'lokakuussa' (in October). Anna lists the months quickly as a curiosity (the names come from nature, e.g. 'lokakuu' is the mud month), glossed, not drilled; only the two months above are practised. Callbacks: 'Kiitos' (episode 2). Alex's careful standard Finnish: he may ask 'Milloin sinun syntymäpäivä on?' and Anna notes the spoken 'sun'. Her flat: warm kitchen, coffee, candles, dark rainy evening at the very end of October.
episodes.illustration_scene: A warm, cosy Finnish home kitchen on a dark rainy evening at the end of October. A round table with a cream layer cake with a few lit candles, two coffee cups and a coffee pot. Anna, a neighbour in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair, is at home in her cream knitted cardigan and blouse, NO coat or scarf, and smiles shyly; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie, raises his coffee cup to her, delighted; his wet yellow raincoat hangs on a hook by the kitchen door. Candles in the window, rain outside. No writing anywhere, no numbers on the cake.
episodes.when: the last day of October, a rainy evening

episodes.title: Mä otan keiton
episodes.description: Alex ja Linnea tulevat sateesta kahvilaan opiskelemaan Linnean tenttiin. Heillä on nälkä. Sanni tunnistaa Alexin. Alex tilaa itse ensimmäistä kertaa lounaan: Mä otan keiton. Ja kahvi, kiitos. Sanni kysyy: Täällä vai mukaan? Linnea auttaa, ja Alex vastaa: Täällä.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide; Sanni has only short service lines. The reason is real: they come in from the rain to study for Linnea's November exam (episode 14) and are hungry; the soup of the day is on the board. In the queue Alex asks Linnea how to say he'll take the soup; she gives the spoken 'Mä otan...' and he tries it for real at the counter. Sanni asks 'Täällä vai mukaan?', which he does not understand; Linnea glosses it quietly and he answers 'Täällä, kiitos'. Sanni recognises him (regular since episode 12). Callbacks: 'Kiitos' (episode 2), the study plan (episode 14). Never say a short Finnish word that is also English on its own (series bible).
episodes.illustration_scene: A warm, cosy Helsinki café on a grey early-November afternoon, already getting dark outside, rain on the big window, wet yellow leaves on the pavement. At the counter Sanni, tall and slim with a sharp dark-brown bob, in her black turtleneck, smiles at Alex; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, in his mustard-yellow rain jacket open over his light-blue hoodie, points at a soup pot; Linnea, blonde ponytail, glasses and freckles, in her lilac raincoat and mint scarf, stands beside him with a book bag. A small menu board with a soup pictogram, no readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: an early November afternoon, grey and rainy, dark by four

episodes.title: Tykkäätkö tästä?
episodes.description: Linnea vie Alexin suomalaiseen lounasravintolaan. Alex näkee karjalanpiirakan ja salmiakkia ensimmäistä kertaa. Hän kysyy: Mitä tässä on? Onko tämä tulista? Linnea nauraa. Alex maistaa: karjalanpiirakasta hän tykkää, salmiakista hän ei tykkää.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide. The reason is real: Linnea takes Alex to a Finnish lunch buffet near the university on a wet November weekday, because he keeps eating the same sandwich at work. At the buffet he points at a karjalanpiirakka and asks 'Mitä tässä on?' (rice inside); he asks 'Onko tämä tulista?' half as a joke, coming from Brazil, and Linnea laughs that Finnish food is almost never spicy. He likes the pie with egg butter ('Tykkään!'). At the till there is a bowl of salmiakki; Linnea dares him, he takes a careful bite and makes a face: 'En tykkää.' Linnea asks 'Tykkäätkö tästä?' each time. Callbacks: 'Mikä tämä on?' (episode 4).
episodes.illustration_scene: A bright, simple Finnish lunch restaurant on a wet November day, rain on the windows, coats on hooks. At a buffet table with soup, salad and a tray of karjalanpiirakka pies, Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie (his mustard-yellow rain jacket on a hook), holds up a small black salmiakki sweet and makes a doubtful face; Linnea, blonde ponytail, glasses and freckles, in her pastel striped sweater, laughs beside him with a plate. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a wet weekday lunchtime in early November

episodes.title: Saisinko laskun?
episodes.description: Ensimmäinen lumi sataa. Alex ja Linnea syövät illalla kahvilassa, jossa on nyt pöytiintarjoilu. Sanni tietää jo Alexin tilauksen. Lopuksi Alex kysyy: Saisinko laskun? Linnea sanoo: Maksetaan erikseen. Alex maksaa kortilla.
episodes.tone: Warm, quietly happy, a first-snow evening
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide; Sanni has only short service lines. The reason is real: the first snow is falling and they stay at the café for its new evening table service; Sanni brings Alex 'the usual' without him ordering, which delights him (callback to episode 2, when he could not order coffee properly). When they want to leave, Alex wants to pay for both to thank Linnea for her help; Linnea says 'Maksetaan erikseen' (Finns usually split). He asks Sanni 'Saisinko laskun?', and when she asks how he pays he answers 'Kortilla'. Sanni asks how the food was; he answers 'Ihan hyvin, kiitos' and Linnea teases that this is a very Finnish compliment. Outside, snow on everything.
episodes.illustration_scene: A cosy Helsinki café in the evening, candles on the tables, the FIRST SNOW falling in big flakes outside the window, yellow street lights, snow just settling on the pavement. THREE people: SANNI, the barista, tall and slim with olive skin and a sharp dark-brown bob, in her black turtleneck, STANDS beside the table and holds a small card payment terminal out towards Alex. ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie, sits at the table and taps his bank card on Sanni's terminal; his navy winter parka and red beanie hang on his chair. LINNEA, blonde braid, glasses and freckles, in her pastel striped sweater, sits across from him with her hands around a coffee cup, smiling; she holds nothing else. Two empty plates and coffee cups on the table. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a mid-November evening, the first snow falling

episodes.title: Missä on maito?
episodes.description: Alex on kaupassa ja etsii maitoa, leipää ja kaurajuomaa. Anna näkee hänet ja auttaa. Alex kysyy: Missä on maito? Anna näyttää. Kassalla on Markku. Markku kysyy: Tarvitsetko kassin? Alex vastaa: Ei kiitos. Markku vitsailee.
episodes.notes: Anna is the guide; Markku has only short service lines. The reason is real: a snowy late-November afternoon, Alex is in the neighbourhood supermarket with a shopping list and cannot find anything, because the shelves are in Finnish; Anna, shopping too, sees him lost. He asks her 'Missä on maito?' (callback to 'Missä on...?' from episode 10) and 'Missä on leipä?'; she shows him, and the oat drink (kaurajuoma) next to the milk, which is what he really wanted. At the till Markku works his other job; he recognises Alex and is warmer now (callback to episode 11, 'Taas sä!'). Markku asks 'Tarvitsetko kassin?'; Alex has his own bag and says 'Ei kiitos'. Markku makes a small dry joke about the snow or the oat drink.
episodes.illustration_scene: A Finnish neighbourhood supermarket on a snowy late-November afternoon, snow visible through the glass doors, wet boot prints on the floor. By a dairy cooler with milk cartons (no readable writing), Anna, a woman in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair with silver streaks, in her long dark-green wool coat and cream knitted hat, points at a shelf and smiles; Alex, a young man with short black curly hair, in his navy padded parka, red beanie and grey scarf, holds a basket with bread and a shopping list. In the background at the till Markku, stocky with short grey hair on the sides, in a work vest over a flannel shirt, waves. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a snowy late-November afternoon

episodes.title: Onko sulla sisaruksia?
episodes.description: Alex on juuri soittanut videopuhelun kotiin Brasiliaan. Puistossa on joulun valot. Alex näyttää Linnealle kuvan perheestään. Linnea kysyy: Onko sulla sisaruksia? Alex vastaa: Minulla on yksi sisko ja kaksi veljeä. Hänen siskollaan on vauva: Hänellä on yksi lapsi. Linnealla on pikkuveli Oulussa.
episodes.tone: Warm, a little homesick, then light
key_phrases: Minulla on yksi sisko ja kaksi veljeä
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide. The reason is real: Alex has just ended a video call home to Brazil (callback to episode 12) and is a little homesick in the December dark; Linnea meets him on the bench under the park's Christmas lights. He shows her a photo of his family on his phone, and the Finnish comes from her questions about the photo. She asks 'Onko sulla sisaruksia?' (spoken 'sulla'); he answers in his careful standard Finnish 'Minulla on yksi sisko ja kaksi veljeä', with her help. His sister just had a baby, so 'Hänellä on yksi lapsi' and he is an uncle now. Linnea has a little brother in Oulu: 'Mulla on pikkuveli', who is annoying but she misses him. Family words (äiti, isä) only glossed in passing. Callbacks: video call home (episode 12), Linnea is from Oulu (episode 7). Never say a short Finnish word that is also English on its own (series bible).
episodes.illustration_scene: A snowy Helsinki park on a dark early-December afternoon, strings of warm white Christmas lights in the bare trees, snow on the ground and benches, a lit street lamp. Alex, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his long dark-navy padded winter parka, red knitted beanie and grey scarf, sits on a bench and holds up his phone showing a family photo (no readable text on the screen); Linnea, blonde braid, glasses and freckles, in her lilac padded winter jacket, cream pompom hat and pastel striped scarf, leans in to look, smiling. Breath steaming in the cold. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: an early-December afternoon, already dark, Christmas lights in the park

episodes.title: Tässä on Leo
episodes.description: Alex ja Linnea ovat joulumarkkinoilla Senaatintorilla. He odottavat Linnean kaveria Leoa, joka on myöhässä. Linnea kuvailee Leoa: Hän on pitkä. Hänellä on oranssi takki. Alex näkee hänet. Leo tulee: Moro! Linnea sanoo: Tässä on mun kaveri Leo. Alex sanoo: Hauska tavata.
episodes.notes: Linnea is the guide; this is Leo's first episode and the first time Alex meets him. The reason is real: Linnea has asked her friend Leo to come to the Christmas market with them, and he is late as usual. The square is crowded, so Linnea describes him so Alex can help spot him: 'Hän on pitkä', 'Hänellä on oranssi takki' (his bright orange puffer jacket). Alex spots him and says it in Finnish. Leo arrives in a rush with a loud 'Moro!' and fast spoken Finnish; Linnea introduces them: 'Tässä on mun kaveri Leo'. Alex answers 'Hauska tavata' and gives his own name. Leo is energetic and forgets to slow down; Linnea tells him to speak slowly (callback to 'Hitaammin, kiitos', episode 3). Glögi in paper cups, Christmas stalls. Nobody uses Leo's name before Linnea says it.
episodes.illustration_scene: The Helsinki Christmas market on Senate Square on a snowy early-December evening: wooden stalls with warm lights, a big lit Christmas tree, the white cathedral steps glowing in the background, people in winter coats, light snow falling. In front, Linnea, blonde braid, glasses and freckles, in her lilac padded winter jacket and cream pompom hat, waves and smiles; Alex, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his dark-navy parka, red beanie and grey scarf, holds a paper cup of glögi; LEO, a tall athletic young man with fair skin and messy reddish-brown hair under a grey beanie, in a bright orange puffer jacket and black neck warmer, arrives grinning with a raised hand. Exactly three main people. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: an early-December evening at the Christmas market, light snow

episodes.title: Onko sulla luistimet?
episodes.description: Viikkoa myöhemmin Leo vie Alexin ulkojäälle luistelemaan. Leo kysyy: Onko sulla luistimet? Alex vastaa: Ei ole. Leo kysyy: Onko sulla aikaa? Alex vastaa: On! He vuokraavat luistimet. Alex kaatuu kerran, mutta nauraa.
episodes.notes: Leo is the guide here (he is a friend now, met in episode 21), but he talks fast in casual spoken Finnish and has to slow down for Alex. The reason is real: a week after the Christmas market Leo bumps into Alex in the street near the park (they have not swapped phone numbers yet; that happens in episode 31) and drags him along to the outdoor ice rink. Leo asks 'Onko sulla luistimet?'; Alex has never skated (he is from Brazil): 'Ei ole.' Leo: 'Onko sulla aikaa?' Alex: 'On!' They rent skates at the rink kiosk. Answer pattern on/ei ole explained by Leo in English, simply. Alex falls once and laughs; Leo helps him up. Leo's slang: 'Moro', 'Joo joo'. Callback: the Christmas market (episode 21).
episodes.illustration_scene: An outdoor ice rink in a snowy Helsinki park on a cold, clear December afternoon, floodlights on, snow banks around the rink, bare trees with a few Christmas lights, a small wooden rental kiosk. LEO, a tall athletic young man with messy reddish-brown hair under a grey beanie, in a bright orange puffer jacket and black neck warmer, glides confidently and reaches a hand out; ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his dark-navy parka, red beanie and grey scarf, wobbles on rental skates, arms out, laughing. Exactly two people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a cold, clear mid-December afternoon at the outdoor ice rink

episodes.title: Tämä on olohuone
episodes.description: Tapaninpäivänä Anna kutsuu Alexin kahville. Alex vietti ensimmäisen joulunsa yksin. Anna näyttää asuntonsa: Tämä on olohuone. Alex kertoo: Asun yksiössä. Hän kysyy: Missä on vessa?
episodes.notes: The day after Christmas (Tapaninpäivä, 26 December). Alex spent his first Christmas alone in Helsinki (his family is in Brazil; he video-called them, callback to episode 12). Anna meets him in the stairwell and invites him up from floor 6 to her flat on floor 4 for coffee and joulutorttu (star-shaped Christmas pastries with plum jam). She shows him round because he asks how big the flats on her floor are: keittiö, olohuone, makuuhuone. Anna asks 'Missä sinä asut?' in a friendly testing way although she knows he lives upstairs; he answers 'Asun yksiössä' (a studio) and explains in English that it is small and has no washing machine (callback to the laundry room in episode 13). Midway he needs the toilet and asks 'Missä on vessa?' for real. Anna explains in English, simply, that 'tämä on' points at a room and that yksiö is a one-room flat. Callbacks: her birthday cake in this kitchen (episode 15), apples from her cottage (episode 8). Indoors, no coats.
episodes.illustration_scene: Inside Anna's warm Finnish apartment on a dark winter afternoon (26 December): a kitchen table in front with a plate of star-shaped joulutorttu pastries and two coffee cups, an open doorway behind leading to a cosy living room with a sofa and candles, snow outside the window, a straw Christmas ornament in the window. On the left, ANNA, a woman in her fifties with shoulder-length brown hair with silver streaks, in her cream knitted cardigan over a light-blue blouse and green trousers, stands and points warmly towards the living-room doorway, smiling. On the right, ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie and dark trousers, sits at the table holding a coffee cup and looks where she points. Both are indoors with no coats, hats or scarves; no coat hangs anywhere. Exactly two people in the whole picture: Anna and Alex, both clearly visible and facing the viewer at three-quarter angle. Nobody else, no one in the living room. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: 26 December (Tapaninpäivä), a dark afternoon in Anna's flat

episodes.title: Mä herään seitsemältä
episodes.description: Tammikuun aamuna kello puoli kahdeksan on vielä pimeää. Linnea ja Alex kävelevät raitiovaunupysäkille. Linnea haukottelee. He kertovat päivästään: Mä herään seitsemältä. Mä juon kahvia. Mä meen töihin. Illalla mä luen.
episodes.notes: Early January, 7:30 a.m., still pitch dark and snowy. Linnea is back from Christmas in Oulu and has started a morning lab course, so for the first time she and Alex leave the building at the same time; they walk together to the tram stop (callback to the tram in episode 10). She yawns; he teases her. They compare their mornings and their usual day because Linnea complains that she now has to wake up early: she says 'Mä herään seitsemältä' (spoken forms, mä/meen). Alex says he drinks coffee first ('Mä juon kahvia'). Then work: 'Mä meen töihin.' Linnea explains in English, simply, that 'meen' is how people say 'menen' and that -ltä after a number means 'at' that hour (callback to telling time, episode 12). The evening: she reads for her course, 'Illalla mä luen.' The tram arrives and the scene ends. Callbacks: her exam in November went well (episode 14), the café study evenings (episode 16).
episodes.illustration_scene: A snowy Helsinki street before sunrise on a dark January morning, streetlights glowing orange, snow banks along the pavement, a green tram stop shelter ahead with a tram's headlights approaching. LINNEA, a young woman with a blonde braid under a cream knitted pompom hat, in a lilac padded winter jacket and pastel striped scarf, yawns behind a mittened hand while walking; ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his dark-navy parka, red beanie and grey scarf, walks beside her holding a takeaway coffee cup, smiling. Exactly two people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: an early January morning at 7:30, still dark, on the way to the tram stop

episodes.title: Mitä sä teet nyt?
episodes.description: Tammikuun iltapäivänä Alex harjoittelee luistelua yksin. Leo juoksee ohi ja pysähtyy. Moro! Mitä sä teet? Alex vastaa: Mä luistelen. Entä sä? Leo: Mä juoksen. Lapset rakentavat lumiukkoa.
episodes.notes: A January afternoon at the outdoor ice rink in the park near Leo's home (callback to episode 22, where Leo taught Alex to skate). Alex now has his own second-hand skates and practises alone, wobbling less. Leo jogs past on the snowy path in running gear and stops when he sees him; they meet by chance because they still have no phone numbers (exchanged only in episode 31). Leo: 'Moro! Mitä sä teet?' (the title is 'Mitä sä teet nyt?' because episode 9 is already 'Mitä sä teet?' about work; Leo can add 'nyt' once to contrast with that episode's 'what do you do for work') Alex: 'Mä luistelen.' Alex asks back 'Entä sä?' Leo: 'Mä juoksen.' Leo explains in English, simply, that 'Mitä sä teet?' asks what someone is doing right now, and that the answer is just mä + the verb. Leo points at kids building a snowman, and Alex tries to say what they are doing; keep extra verbs inside full phrases, never alone. Alex shows he can skate backwards a little; Leo is impressed, then has to keep running before he gets cold. Leo's slang: 'Moro', 'Joo joo'. Never say a short word like 'Entä' alone: keep 'Entä sä?' together.
episodes.illustration_scene: An outdoor ice rink in a snowy Helsinki park on a grey January afternoon, low pale sun, snow banks around the rink, bare trees, a few children building a snowman in the background, small and out of focus. LEO, a tall athletic young man with messy reddish-brown hair under a grey beanie, in black running tights, his bright orange puffer jacket and black neck warmer, stands on the snowy path just outside the rink's low boards, jogging on the spot in black running shoes (he is NOT on the ice and wears NO skates); ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his dark-navy parka, red beanie and grey scarf, glides towards him on skates, arms slightly out, proud. Exactly two people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a grey January afternoon at the outdoor ice rink

episodes.title: Mikä sun harrastus on?
episodes.description: Tammikuun lopussa Alex kokeilee kiipeilyä urheiluhallissa. Leo on siellä kiipeilyporukkansa kanssa. Mikä sun harrastus on? Mä kiipeilen. Alex tykkää pelata, mutta ei tykkää juosta.
episodes.notes: A dark Thursday evening in late January at an indoor climbing wall in a sports centre. Alex has come to a beginners' evening (a colleague told him about it) and stands at the bottom of the wall in rental climbing shoes, unsure. Leo is there with his Thursday climbing group and drops down from the wall; they meet by chance again because they still have no phone numbers (they swap them only in episode 31). Indoors: no coats. Leo asks 'Mikä sun harrastus on?' and answers his own question: 'Mä kiipeilen.' Leo explains in English that 'harrastus' is a hobby and that the answer is simply mä + the verb. Alex says his hobbies are video games and cooking Brazilian food: he learns 'Mä tykkään pelata.' (Leo explains that 'tykkään' is the everyday way to say 'I like', followed by the basic verb). Leo, the runner from episode 25, asks if Alex likes running; Alex: 'Mä en tykkää juosta.' Leo laughs and teases that Alex at least likes skating now (callback to 22 and 25). Alex can say 'Mä tykkään luistella.' End: Leo talks him into trying the easy green route; Alex climbs two holds and is proud. Leo's slang: 'Moro', 'Joo joo'. Every line is all Finnish or all English: when Leo explains a Finnish word, the English explanation is one line and the Finnish word is its own line. Never say a short Finnish word alone; keep 'Mä tykkään pelata.' and 'Mä en tykkää juosta.' whole.
episodes.illustration_scene: An indoor climbing gym in a Helsinki sports centre on a dark winter evening, a tall wall covered in colourful plastic holds, thick blue crash mats on the floor, black windows showing night outside. LEO, a tall athletic young man with messy reddish-brown hair under his grey beanie, in a faded band t-shirt and black sports trousers, chalk on his hands, stands on the mat grinning and pointing up at the wall; ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie and dark trousers, wears rental climbing shoes and looks up at the wall, unsure but smiling. No coats. Exactly two people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a dark Thursday evening in late January at an indoor climbing wall

episodes.title: Mitä sä teet viikonloppuna?
episodes.title_en: What are you doing at the weekend?
episodes.description: Perjantai-iltapäivänä Alex ja Linnea istuvat Sannin kahvilassa. Mitä sä teet viikonloppuna? Lauantaina Linnea hiihtää. Sunnuntaina Alex lepää. Kiva!
episodes.notes: A snowy Friday afternoon at the end of January, already dark at four, at Sanni's café (their study place since episode 16; Sanni has no lines in this episode). Indoors: coats hang on the chair backs. Linnea's lab course week is over and she is in a good mood. Present tense only (Finnish uses the present for plans), so no past tense anywhere. Linnea asks 'Mitä sä teet viikonloppuna?' and explains in English that 'viikonloppuna' means 'at the weekend'. She answers: 'Lauantaina mä hiihdän.' She is going cross-country skiing in Paloheinä with friends from her course. Alex has never skied; she explains 'hiihtää' is cross-country skiing, Finland's favourite winter sport. Alex: Saturday evening he has the building's sauna slot (callback to Anna's sauna evenings in episode 13), and on Sunday he rests and video-calls his family in Brazil (episode 12): 'Sunnuntaina mä lepään.' Linnea: 'Kiva!' and explains it is the everyday word for 'nice'. Alex then says his whole weekend in Finnish with lauantaina and sunnuntaina. End: Linnea says maybe one day he can try skiing too; Alex: 'Ehkä.' (sets up episode 28). Every line is all Finnish or all English; never a Finnish word inside an English line. Keep 'Kiva!' as its own Finnish line, never alone in English.
episodes.illustration_scene: A warm, cosy Helsinki café on a dark, snowy late-January afternoon, big window with snow falling outside and streetlights glowing, candles on the tables. At a window table LINNEA, a young woman with freckles, glasses and long blonde hair in a ponytail, in a colourful knitted sweater, mimes cross-country skiing with both arms, laughing; ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his light-blue hoodie, holds a coffee cup and laughs. Their winter jackets hang on the chair backs (her lilac jacket, his dark-navy parka). Exactly two people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: a dark, snowy Friday afternoon at the end of January at the café

episodes.title: Mennäänkö luistelemaan?
episodes.description: Helmikuun alussa Alex, Linnea ja Leo tapaavat puistossa. Mennäänkö luistelemaan lauantaina? Joo, mennään! Ehkä. Ei, valitettavasti. He sopivat: kello kaksi kentällä.
episodes.notes: Early February at dusk by the outdoor ice rink in the park near Leo's home (episodes 22 and 25), floodlights coming on. Alex and Linnea are walking home through the park and meet Leo, who is out running again. Leo has the idea: 'Mennäänkö luistelemaan lauantaina?' He explains in English that 'Mennäänkö...?' means 'Shall we go...?'. Linnea at once: 'Joo, mennään!' Alex hesitates because Saturday afternoon he may have a video call home: 'Ehkä.' Linnea explains 'ehkä' means 'maybe'. Leo then asks Linnea if she wants to go running with him on Sunday morning and she laughs: 'Ei, valitettavasti.' (she explains 'valitettavasti' means 'unfortunately', the polite no). Alex then checks his phone, the call is in the evening, so he says 'Joo, mennään!' too. They agree: Saturday at two, at the rink ('Kello kaksi!', callback to the time in episode 12). End: Alex asks how he can tell them if he is late, and they realise none of them have each other's phone numbers; Leo laughs that next time they swap numbers (sets up episode 31). Every line is all Finnish or all English; never a Finnish word inside an English line. Keep 'Ei, valitettavasti.' and 'Joo, mennään!' whole, never 'Ei' or 'Joo' alone.
episodes.illustration_scene: The outdoor ice rink in a snowy Helsinki park at dusk in early February, deep blue sky, floodlights just switching on over the ice, snow banks and bare trees, a few skaters small in the background. On the snowy path by the low boards: LEO, a tall athletic young man with FAIR, pale Nordic skin, light freckles and messy reddish-brown (ginger) hair under his grey beanie, clean-shaven, in his bright orange puffer jacket and black neck warmer, in black running shoes, points at the ice with a big grin; LINNEA, a young woman with a blonde braid under a cream knitted pompom hat, in her lilac padded winter jacket and pastel striped scarf, gives a thumbs-up; ALEX, a young man with light brown skin and short black curly hair, in his dark-navy parka, red beanie and grey scarf, shrugs with a hesitant smile. Exactly three people in front. No readable writing anywhere.
episodes.when: early February at dusk by the outdoor ice rink in the park
